description: Records are held in paper files, registers, Excel, and Word; no integrated spatial system.
design_implication: Build a staged migration from paper/Excel; do not assume born-digital data.

description: Departments keep and update their own records; coordination is by file, phone, and direct contact.
design_implication: Create data custodians and a cross-department governance group.

description: Addresses are manual and inconsistent; National ID is used for identity, not location.
design_implication: Make the address gazetteer the first foundation layer.

description: RCC lacks a cadastral database; holding/tax records cannot be reliably linked to buildings or parcels.
design_implication: Separate holding_no, parcel_id, building_id, and address_id; build link tables.

description: No shared spatial asset register; as-built data filed but not linked to assets.
design_implication: Use an asset registry, asset_no, and as-built handover workflow.

description: Field staff use paper instructions and paper returns; no mobile forms or GPS.
design_implication: Use QField/mobile forms with offline capture, photos, and accuracy fields.

description: Most staff have no GIS, Excel, or data-management training; IT support is limited.
design_implication: Budget for training, champions, and ongoing support.

description: Participants want a Spatial Services Unit, departmental custodians, standards, and data policy.
design_implication: Adopt the RACI, data policy, and stewardship model.

description: Personal, tax, identity, and complaint data should be restricted and access-controlled.
design_implication: Use access classification, role-based access, audit, and pub views.

description: Public map should show services, roads, facilities, waste areas, and approved planning information.
design_implication: Publish selective layers only after review.

description: Trust depends on accuracy, source, date, update frequency, and error reporting.
design_implication: Record provenance, metadata, QA status, data date, and correction channel.

description: Governance first, then central database/GIS, address layer, training, workflows, and public map.
design_implication: Follow the phased roadmap and decision gates.

description: Inaccurate data, no maintenance, unclear responsibilities, no training, weak privacy, no funding, political influence.
design_implication: Design maintenance, governance, training, and financing from the start.

description: RDA shares planning data case by case; no shared platform, standards, or catalogue.
design_implication: Use data-sharing agreements, common catalogue, and metadata standards.

description: Bangla and English, plain language, symbols, low bandwidth, mobile, print, and training.
design_implication: Design bilingual, low-bandwidth, mobile-friendly public access.

description: Citizens visit councilor/ward offices; no integrated online system or public map.
design_implication: Keep multiple channels; do not make the map the only access route.

description: Limited interest, political influence, short-term plans, and uneven staff capacity.
design_implication: Build executive sponsorship and change management.

description: Duplicates and conflicts are resolved manually through documents, calls, and site visits.
design_implication: Use domains, unique IDs, validation rules, and audit history.
